changes: Helios II reset: Galaxy walked away from a summer deal because the wrap offered did not give investment-grade protection to debt and equity. The search now targets IG hyperscalers or credit-enhanced tenants, with no fixed date (2028 data halls, power around mid-2028).

CoreWeave exposure clarified: the Helios I leases sit with CoreWeave's parent, behind site-level GPU lenders; the load is allocated to an IG hyperscaler for now. Cash rent and the -$152mn working-capital swing went undiscussed.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Galaxy as a crypto franchise with a contracted Helios annuity underneath; at about $17 the price roughly equals contracted Helios value, so the debate is whether CoreWeave's credit stress makes that annuity worth less than the sell side assumes.
headline: No change to the consensus view in direction: the call confirmed the Phase I annuity and the 2027 ramp and showed discipline on Helios II credit, but pushed the Helios II catalyst out and left cash rent from CoreWeave unaddressed, so long-term compounding holds while credit quality still rests on one sub-investment-grade parent.
kona: The call shows how a landlord prices tenant credit: Galaxy walked away from a Helios II deal because an investment-grade wrap did not protect its debt and equity, and it now admits its CoreWeave leases sit at the parent, behind site-level GPU lenders. Kona should ask any GPU tenant for direct or wrapped credit at the entity that owns the chips, or prepaid rent covering debt service through the build, and price construction carry into rent (Galaxy's ~$198 per kW-month, grid-powered and near-triple-net, is a ceiling). Galaxy's own uncontracted 830 MW will not energize before mid-2028, so time-to-power remains Kona's edge.
monitor: 10-Q (due within weeks): cash rent received from CoreWeave, the deferred or straight-line rent balance, and what drove the -$152mn Data Centers working-capital outflow.
Texas audit results (December) and Batch Zero allocations (around April 2027): they set Helios II-IV timing and the next tenant conversation.
Phase III debt in 1H27 (loan-to-cost, coupon vs 9.875% on Phase II) and repayment of the $445mn exchangeable in December from cash.

sections.body: Matrix: every topic is 'new' (first transcript held). Nine of fourteen questions touched Helios, funding or power; five were crypto or tokenization. Nobody asked about cash rent, the working-capital outflow or tenant security, and management did not pre-empt them. Prepared remarks pre-empted the Phase II revenue footnote and the exchangeable. Trevor's watch-list. Analyst chosen: Jonathan Petersen (Jefferies), the most credit-focused questioner (lender appetite and covenants); also tracking James Yaro (Goldman Sachs) on capital priorities. 3Q26: Petersen asked whether tighter lender terms affect existing facilities or the next raise; answer partial (existing facilities unaffected, lenders 'a lot more conservative', no terms). Later evidence to log: Phase III debt terms in 1H27. Open items: cash rent and receivable; tenant security; Phase III loan-to-cost; exchangeable repaid in cash; Helios II tenant credit; December audit.
